findings.fact: stream_openai_responses allocates and emits a fresh response_id in response.created before handle_openai_responses can discover any durable replay. If handle later returns a stored response, the stream can expose one id in response.created and another in response.completed/tool output.
findings.required_fix: Make the durable replay decision while holding the same conversation/turn serialization boundary and before the first SSE byte. On replay, emit the stored payload directly; on fresh work, allocate response_id only after replay miss is known. Preserve existing lock order to avoid deadlock.

findings.fact: ConversationSegmentStore._save_locked catches FilesystemOwnershipError/OSError, sets _persistence_blocked, and returns no success/failure signal. put therefore cannot tell server.py whether progress+replay actually reached disk before a tool call is exposed to Codex.
findings.required_fix: Return an explicit durable publication result (or raise a dedicated error) and fail closed before exposing a tool-call response when the atomic segment+replay record was not durably published. Roll back the just-installed in-memory replacement on failed publication so an undurable replay cannot masquerade as durable.

findings.fact: response_input_fingerprints mixes request context into each input item, but an empty input produces an empty tuple. Tuple equality alone is therefore insufficient as the exact replay key for zero-item requests.
findings.required_fix: Persist response_input_fingerprint(body) as a separate replay_request_fingerprint and use it for exact replay identity; keep input_fingerprints only for prefix/continuation semantics.

candidate_record.state_version_policy: Do not blindly invalidate v2. Legacy records must remain detectable so exact progress-without-replay can fail closed rather than silently re-infer.
